evidence.locator: Introduction, onion tissue disruption and organosulfur pathway
evidence.evidence_summary: Onion tissue disruption brings cysteine sulfoxides into contact with alliinase, producing sulfenic acids and downstream volatile sulfur chemistry.
evidence.limitations: Analytical chemistry study; used here for pathway description.

evidence.evidence_summary: 2002 Nature communication showed the lachrymatory factor is specifically synthesized by a previously undiscovered lachrymatory-factor synthase.
LFS catalyzes production of syn-propanethial S-oxide and later structural/biochemical work investigated its catalytic mechanism.
evidence.limitations: Mechanistic details are simplified for a general audience.

evidence.locator: Why do onions make you cry? / reflex tears
evidence.evidence_summary: Eye irritation from onion exposure triggers reflex tears that help flush irritating material.
evidence.limitations: Clinical educational reference rather than primary onion biochemistry.

evidence.locator: Introduction and results on LFS-suppressed onion
evidence.evidence_summary: Suppressing LFS activity produces tearless/non-pungent onion lines and redirects sulfur chemistry.
evidence.limitations: Experimental lines are not representative of every commercial onion.

evidence.evidence_summary: Onion lachrymatory chemistry is discussed as part of sulfur-based chemical defense and pungency chemistry.
evidence.limitations: Defense interpretation is broader than any single compound's ecological effect.
